trailhead.name: Twin Lakes (Robinson Creek / Barney Lake trailhead)

identifiedBy.fact: route text: from Twin Lakes through Kerrick Canyon to Seavey Pass

otherFacts.value: Twin Lakes, Barney Lake, Peeler Lake, Kerrick Meadow, Rancheria Creek, Seavey Pass; camp ~8,500 ft below east slope
~18 mi from trailhead to camp below Piute (3 days)

notes: Route text names Twin Lakes; a 2019 report from Twin Lakes confirms the start (that party reached the SE ridge, not the NE ridge). Twin Lakes has two USFS points about 1 km apart (Robinson Creek 38.1468,-119.3898; Horse Creek 38.1437,-119.3787). The Barney Lake/Robinson Creek trail is the Kerrick route, so Robinson Creek chosen. Single placement; no page printed a coordinate. SummitPost 403.

trailhead.name: Rocky Canyon pullout on US 50 (informal start, not a signed trailhead)

identifiedBy.fact: Rocky Canyon route starts at a roadside pullout on US 50 just past the Rocky Canyon creek, before Twin Bridges; trail up a dirt bank across the road

otherFacts.value: trail also starts ~150 yd east of creek near mile 59.0 marker (green T on rock)

notes: Re-read the Outbound page this pass: confirms pullout and coordinate. Two coordinates agree within ~90 m (second from earlier pass, not re-opened). Not a land-manager point; Pyramid Creek TH (USFS 38.8117,-120.1237) is a different route.

otherFacts.value: Taboose Pass (closest per SummitPost summary), Sawmill, Baxter; also Road's End (Cedar Grove) 16 h round trip

notes: Several equally used starts: Taboose Pass (climber.org 2016/1872), Roads End/Cedar Grove via Paradise Valley (Burd trip report, fetched, ~16 h round trip), Sawmill and Baxter passes. Nothing ties 'Standard route' to one. SummitPost 403. Taboose is the nearest-by-trail but this is inference only.

trailhead.name: Bear Ridge Trailhead (Lake Thomas Edison dam overlook)

identifiedBy.fact: Burd SPS trip report starts at Bear Ridge TH near Lake Edison dam overlook, Bear Ridge Cutoff to JMT junction, cross-country to SW arete; SummitPost summary also calls Bear Ridge the normal route

otherFacts.value: class 3 SW arete via Bear Ridge, JMT junction, snow survey cabin, two lakes NW of the arete

notes: Moderate. Bear Ridge is the normal route per Burd's report and the SummitPost summary (summary only; page 403). Alternative: Bear Creek Diversion Dam by OHV road (4WD), Mosquito Flat from the east. USFS 'Bear Ridge Cutoff' point is a trail point near the lot, the signed TH is near the dam overlook; placement is approximate. Wikipedia has no trailhead info.

identifiedBy.fact: Burd report of the West Face: Sawtooth TH, Glacier Pass, Hands and Knees Pass, Little Five Lakes, Big Arroyo, then cross-country N to cirque lakes and West Face

otherFacts.value: 2000+ from Big Arroyo to cirque lakes; ~3500 Big Arroyo back to TH
6 h to base, 10 h to summit from Big Arroyo

notes: Weak-to-moderate: the report describes this exact west-face route and starts at Sawtooth, and the SummitPost summary says Mineral King is the nearest trailhead to Big Arroyo. Big Arroyo is also reachable from Crescent Meadow via the High Sierra Trail (~30 mi), a legitimate alternative. Multi-day backpack. One NPS placement only.

trailhead.name: Cielo Vista Ranch Four Way junction (walk starts here; ranch HQ is the check-in)

identifiedBy.fact: climb13ers North Ridge page: Cielo Vista TH, practical start at the Four-Way road junction, climb Culebra first then the connecting ridge to Red

placements.name: Cielo Vista Ranch HQ trailhead (check-in), 9,100 ft

otherFacts.value: 8.2 round trip from four-way, including Culebra
HQ to four-way 3.4 mi easy 4WD; upper trailhead at 4.4 mi (37.139,-105.2157) if allowed

notes: Private ranch; the only placement source is climb13ers (DMS converted). The four-way is the practical start and shared by Culebra, Red and others; the sign-in HQ is ~5 km west. Land is private, so no land-manager point exists.

otherFacts.value: Red Mountain (#1033) PCT trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass, 47.4278,-121.4134, west slope

notes: No readable page about the east side. WTA describes only the west slope from the PCT/Commonwealth Basin; SummitPost east-side pages (red-mountain-from-its-east/90320, east-ridge-from-red-mtn-pass) returned 403. Search summaries mention a Mountaineers option via Cave Ridge from Alpental and Snow Lake, none verified. Probable (weak, inferred): PCT North TH like the standard route.

Same as East Face. A SummitPost page titled 'East Ridge from Red Mtn Pass' exists (403), which suggests it starts from the PCT/Commonwealth Basin side to Red Pass, but this was not read, so not evidence. Probable: PCT North TH (47.428012,-121.413484).
Same as East Face. Search summary (not opened) says the SE face is Class 4 and its SummitPost page is a 2002 east-side climb; page 403. Probable: PCT North TH, unverified.

identifiedBy.fact: Red Peak summit climb starts at Mono Meadows TH: follow trail toward Red Peak Pass ~1/4 mile, leave it at a granite bench and climb red talus to the summit

otherFacts.value: downclimb to a small pass NW of the peak, return over 'Reddy Pass' to the trail
Secor: over Red Peak Pass with exposed 3rd class on the north side

notes: Good: a report of the summit climb itself starts here (re-read this pass). Ottoway/Red Peak Pass loop corroborated by a second trip report (mytrailmixx). Single placement (NPS).

identifiedBy.fact: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft)

summitEvidence.fact: descent text starts 'From the summit' and overview climbs Rock Mountain's northeast side

otherFacts.value: Merritt Lake TH is ~3 mi east of the Rock Lake TH; old forest road to it is rough
47.7757,-120.9581 (WTA), 2,675 ft, off US 2 just past mile 73

notes: Trailhead named by route text; the only placement is the USFS 'Merritt Lake Trailhead' (the route says 'Old'; the old road start may sit a little lower than this point, ~2,950 ft stated). WTA pages do not give Merritt Lake coordinates; wenatcheeoutdoors 403. Descent ends at the Rock Mountain TH (USFS 47.775232,-120.957772; WTA 47.7757,-120.9581, agreeing within ~60 m), a different trailhead, so a shuttle is needed.
